items.label: 1C
items.claim: German statutory NIPT volume was still ramping hard in 2024, rising from about 32% to nearly 50% of pregnancies, so the NIPT-maturing drag is not yet visible in Germany.
items.detail: The Bundestag motion cites BARMER data: on average almost 50% of pregnant women used NIPT in 2024, against 32% in 2023, a gain of about 18 points. The hib summary of 29 Jan 2026 reports this and the motion text is not independently verified. The 32% figure comes only from the Drucksache, and a separate expert opinion gives about 48% of pregnancies for 2022–2024. At about 680K births, 50% uptake is roughly 340K tests. At 1–2 Gb per test that is about 0.34–0.68M Gb a year, which is only about 0.04–0.07% of Illumina's HT Gb (~1 billion Gb/yr, our approximation). Germany is therefore a watch-out for the thesis, but tiny in volume terms.
items.quote: nearly 50% of pregnant women used NIPT in 2024
items.why_new: It quantifies the 2023→2024 jump (32%→~50%) and the motion's cited figures, where the known list only says uptake was ~50% with headroom.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: German NIPT uptake is already about 80% among women over 40 and about half among those under 36, so the high-intensity cohorts are near saturation and future growth must come from the young cohort.
items.detail: A search-result summary of the bifg/BARMER paper in Gynäkologische Praxis 2026 (snippet, I could not render the PDF) gives 2025 uptake of about one in three pregnant women under 26, about one in two under 36, and about 80% over 40, with rates rising in all age groups. The Drucksache-era figures were about 25% for under-26s and 75% for over-40s in 2024. The gains are one-third of a point to five points a year in the oldest groups, so they are nearing a ceiling. Growth now depends on lower-risk, lower-depth young women.
items.source_name: bifg / BARMER, Gynäkologische Praxis 2026 (via search summary)
items.why_new: The known list has no age-specific German uptake, and these figures show the 40+ cohort is near its ceiling.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: The Bundestag motion and the BARMER analysis create a policy overhang: the false-positive rate is reportedly four times what is expected, invasive tests have risen, and monitoring is due by end-June 2027.
items.detail: The cross-party motion (CDU/CSU, SPD, Greens, Left) asks for monitoring of the G-BA coverage decision, results to the Bundestag by 30 Jun 2027, and an interdisciplinary expert panel. It cites a false-positive rate in routine care about 4x the theoretical rate, invasive tests rising by 0.1–2.5 per 1,000 pregnancies instead of falling, and women skipping first-trimester screening after a negative NIPT. These findings could be used to tighten the G-BA indication, which would cap German NIPT volume after 2027. Germany's Gb exposure is small, but the same narrative could spread to other European payers.
items.source_name: Bundestag Drucksache 21/3873 (via hib and search summary)
items.why_new: It adds the specific cited harms (4x false positives, higher invasive-test counts) and the three asks; the known list only has the monitoring deadline.

items.label: 1C
items.claim: NIPT in Germany has become de facto screening although the G-BA did not set it up as routine care, which makes the indication a target for restriction.
items.detail: The bifg study authors say that after coverage began on 1 Jul 2022, NIPT became a screening test although it is not part of routine care. A search summary of the bifg analysis (766,245 pregnancies, 30,365 with a billed NIPT, data to about Mar 2024) says the study shows no fall in invasive tests. Caritas/SkF has also asked for scientific monitoring. Regulatory pressure on indication and uptake is therefore building in the country with the largest statutory insurer population.
items.why_new: It adds third-party advocacy pressure and the study sample sizes behind the policy risk.

notes: I could not read the Gynäkologische Praxis PDF or the Drucksache body, because WebFetch returned only metadata and PDF page rendering failed (no poppler). The quarterly Table 2 and the Abb. 1 chart values are therefore not extracted. All numbers above come from the hib summary and search-result snippets. The Gb exposure is small, so the value is directional.
